validity_note: True. app.payments.enabled binds to ${APP_PAYMENTS_ENABLED:false} and no deployment file sets it. A company is a User with UserType.COMPANY, and CompanySubscription is 1:1 on user_id. There is no per-company or per-tenant flag mechanism; every gate is global.

key_facts.claim: The switch works only at startup. SubscriptionPaidController, StripeWebhookController, StripeConfig (the only Stripe.apiKey assignment), InvoiceRetryCronJob, InvoiceCreatedEventListener and TrialExpiryNotifierCronJob all use @ConditionalOnProperty(havingValue=true, matchIfMissing=false). It cannot vary per company, so a pilot needs these beans on globally.

PaymentsDisabledBootGuard loads only when the property equals false. At @PostConstruct it throws if any row is TRIAL_ENTERPRISE, BUSINESS_ACTIVE, ENTERPRISE_ACTIVE, DOWNGRADE_PENDING, PAYMENT_FAILED or TERMS_PENDING; terminal statuses are ignored. With the flag OFF, one paying pilot company means a startup crash-loop.

The runtime guard is a no-arg global check, requirePaymentsEnabled(). It runs at the top of activateTrial, initiateUpgrade, requestDowngrade, cancelDowngrade and all five webhook handlers, and throws PaymentsDisabledException (503). getStatus, the cron processors and deactivateForAccountDeletion skip it. This is the natural per-company choke point, but it has no userId today.

SubscriptionPeriodProcessorCronJob is always registered: it runs processExpiredTrials and processExpiredDowngrades only when the flag is on, and FREE period rollover always. TermsGraceProcessorCronJob returns early when the flag is off; otherwise it suspends TERMS_PENDING rows past their grace deadline and cancels their Stripe subscriptions. Neither is scoped to companies.

The webhook verifies the signature, then routes five event types. Handlers find the company only by stripeCustomerId or stripeSubscriptionId under pessimistic locks, so rows without Stripe IDs are untouchable. Any exception except an optimistic-lock conflict is logged and acked 200, so Stripe never retries it.

handleInvoicePaid creates an InvoiceRecord and publishes InvoiceCreatedEvent only when amountPaid > 0. The gated listener and cron call InvoiceRetryService, which is always registered, needs CompanyData (NIP and address) and uses idempotency key cio-<id>. FakturowniaAdapter is an ungated bean that does nothing unless fakturownia is enabled and has an API key.

The FE reads the flag only from anonymous GET /public-config (permitAll, no-store), which returns the global value. PublicConfigApiService caches it with shareReplay and fails open to true. plan-billing hides trial, cancel-trial, portal and the plan ladder behind it, and layout probes /subscription/status for the trial nudge only when it is true.

/subscription/* is @Hidden from OpenAPI, so the FE uses hand-written subscription.client.ts and hidden-models.ts, and a new per-company status field will not arrive through codegen. getStatus computes trialEligible without looking at the flag.

Every test profile sets app.payments.enabled=true. The OFF path runs only in the payments-off-tests Failsafe fork (RunPaymentsDisabledIT), and PaymentsTogglePresence_IntegrationTest pins the per-mode bean sets.

gaps.finding: The flag defaults disagree. AppPaymentsProperties defaults to true, but the bean gates use matchIfMissing=false and the boot guard needs an explicit false. If the property is absent, the paid beans are off while requirePaymentsEnabled passes, /public-config says true and both crons run paid branches.

Plan limits are global rows, and the rollout raised FREE to 5, the same as BUSINESS. A pilot BUSINESS upgrade buys no campaigns, and changing the limits hits every company. The FE ladder still hard-codes 2/5/10.

The TERMS_PENDING lifecycle is unwired: enterTermsPending and acceptTerms are called only from TestSubscriptionController, yet TermsGraceProcessorCronJob acts on such rows for all companies once payments are on.
The FE gating is incomplete: the PAYMENT_FAILED portal button and the pending-downgrade cancel button are not behind paymentsEnabled(), and the signal starts as true.
The server does not enforce subscription consent: SubscriptionService has no LegalConsentService, and only the FE orders the consent call before trial or upgrade.

invariants: Non-pilot companies behave exactly as today: FREE_ACTIVE with limit 5, paid actions refused, no Stripe customer, no invoices, no paid buttons or trial nudge.
No non-pilot company can reach an in-flight paid status, and a startup or scheduled check keeps enforcing that.
Webhook safety stays: event-id dedupe and unique constraint, locks, 503 on lock conflict; no pilot event is acked and dropped.
At most one Fakturownia invoice per paid InvoiceRecord (cio-<id>), and only when amountPaid > 0.
Anonymous /public-config keeps its global meaning; per-company entitlement is exposed only to the authenticated company.
Removing a company from the pilot, or turning payments off, first reconciles its Stripe subscription and status, so the app still boots.
good_designs: Treat app.payments.enabled=true as the infrastructure switch and add a DB-backed, admin-managed per-company entitlement, checked by requirePaymentsEnabled(userId) on every user-initiated paid path, exposed on /subscription/status (mirrored in hidden-models.ts) to drive plan-billing and layout, plus a pilot-aware check that no non-pilot row is paid.

Replace the boolean with a mode (OFF | PILOT | ON) and an allowlist: beans register for PILOT and ON, the boot guard covers all rows in OFF and non-pilot rows in PILOT, and /public-config stays false for anonymous users.

Order the work as: entitlement, guard and tests while the flag stays OFF; then the status field and FE gating; then plan limits; then turn the infrastructure on in staging with Stripe test keys; then production.
red_flags: Setting APP_PAYMENTS_ENABLED=true is enough: that opens the paid endpoints and trial nudge to every COMPANY, drops the boot guard and tells every visitor paymentsEnabled=true.
Keep the flag false and exempt pilot companies in SubscriptionService: the paid controller, webhook, StripeConfig and invoice beans would be absent, and the boot guard crash-loops.
app.payments.enabled can vary per company or per request: every gate is @ConditionalOnProperty, evaluated once at startup.
Serve a per-company flag from /public-config, or rely on OpenAPI codegen for the new field: the endpoint is anonymous and FE-cached, and /subscription/* is @Hidden.
The boot guard rejects any non-FREE_ACTIVE row (as the stale Liquibase comment says), or FakturowniaAdapter and InvoiceRetryService are gated by the payments flag.

architecture.today: app.payments.enabled (AppPaymentsProperties) selects paid beans via @ConditionalOnProperty at startup; when false, a @PostConstruct guard blocks boot on in-flight paid rows.
architecture.fit: Keeps the property, or a mode in that class, as the infrastructure switch and extends the guard to non-pilot rows.
architecture.breaks: A new env flag or flag library, beans expected to vary per company, or a dropped guard.

architecture.today: requirePaymentsEnabled() opens paid service and webhook methods and throws PaymentsDisabledException, sent as 503 with messageKey.
architecture.fit: Becomes requirePaymentsEnabled(userId) on user-initiated paid paths, using the userId the COMPANY controllers resolve.
architecture.breaks: A filter, interceptor or aspect with its own allowlist, or a company id from the request.

architecture.today: The handler dedupes on stripe_event_id, services lock rows by Stripe ids, lock conflicts get 503 and other errors are acked 200.
architecture.fit: Pilot events reuse this path under the global check, so none is refused per company and acked.
architecture.breaks: A second webhook route or Stripe account, or a per-company throw that is acked and lost.

architecture.today: Crons use @Scheduled with @SchedulerLock, always-on ones checking the flag inline; invoices flow via InvoiceCreatedEvent, an AFTER_COMMIT listener, a retry cron and InvoicingPort.
architecture.fit: Keeps jobs global, scopes paid processor queries to pilot companies, and leaves invoicing unchanged.
architecture.breaks: Per-company or unlocked schedulers, or a direct or pilot-gated Fakturownia call.

architecture.today: Billing state is the @Version CompanySubscription row (1:1 on user_id); schema changes are dated SQL changesets with rollback lines, included from changelog.xml.
architecture.fit: Stores pilot membership beside company_subscription via a changeset, set by an ADMIN endpoint and readable by guard and cron queries.
architecture.breaks: Membership in Firebase claims, Redis or a flag service that repository queries cannot read.

architecture.today: PublicConfigApiService caches the anonymous global flag that plan-billing and layout gate on; @Hidden /subscription uses hand-written api-frozen clients behind core wrappers.
architecture.fit: Adds the entitlement to authenticated /subscription/status and hidden-models.ts and gates the UI on it.
architecture.breaks: A per-company value in /public-config, raw HttpClient calls in feature code, or relying on openapi:gen.
